title: Alma takes up the teaching
summary: Seeing that Amulek’s words have silenced Zeezrom and that Zeezrom has begun to tremble, Alma begins speaking to him, establishing Amulek’s words and unfolding the scriptures further. The surrounding multitude hears him.

explicit_facts.text: Amulek’s words have silenced Zeezrom, and Zeezrom begins to tremble under a consciousness of his guilt.
Alma begins speaking to Zeezrom to establish Amulek’s words and unfold the scriptures further.
The surrounding people hear Alma’s words, and the multitude is great.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma and Zeezrom are within speaking distance.
The multitude is within hearing distance.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise location, clothing, ages, and arrangement of the crowd.

narration.text: Now the words that Alma spake unto Zeezrom were heard by the people round about;

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Amulek’s earlier words as a new present action.

title: Alma exposes Zeezrom’s plan
summary: Alma addresses Zeezrom and the people, declaring that Zeezrom lied to God and describing his plan to turn the people against Alma and Amulek. He calls it a snare of the adversary.

explicit_facts.text: Alma tells Zeezrom that he lied to God and that his thoughts are known through God's Spirit.
Alma describes Zeezrom's plan to turn the people against Alma and Amulek and have them reviled and cast out.
Alma says the plan was of Zeezrom's adversary and tells the gathered people to remember his words.
Alma calls the plan a snare meant to bring the people into subjection and everlasting destruction.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma speaks audibly to Zeezrom and the gathered people.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible manifestation of the adversary, chains, or a snare.

spoken_dialogue.text: Now Zeezrom, seeing that thou hast been taken in thy lying and craftiness, for thou hast not lied unto men only but thou hast lied unto God;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma (son of Alma)

spoken_dialogue.text: Now I would that ye should remember that what I say unto thee I say unto all.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma (son of Alma)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The chains and snare are figurative teaching, not literal visible objects.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the devil or literal chains as present.

title: Zeezrom trembles and asks
summary: Zeezrom trembles more and becomes convinced of God's power and Alma and Amulek's knowledge of his heart. He diligently asks Alma about resurrection and judgment.

explicit_facts.text: Zeezrom trembles more exceedingly and is convinced of God's power and of Alma and Amulek's knowledge of his thoughts and intents.
Zeezrom diligently inquires about the kingdom of God and asks Alma what Amulek meant concerning resurrection and judgment according to works.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Zeezrom visibly trembles as he addresses Alma.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible supernatural sign or depiction of Zeezrom's thoughts.

spoken_dialogue.text: What does this mean which Amulek hath spoken concerning the resurrection of the dead, that all shall rise from the dead, both the just and the unjust, and are brought to stand before God to be judged according to their works?

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Do not depict resurrection or judgment as a current event; Zeezrom asks about them.
prohibited_inventions: Do not visualize thoughts as readable images or symbols.

title: The portion of the word
summary: Alma expounds to a man that knowledge of God's mysteries is granted according to heed and diligence. He contrasts the portions of the word received by those who harden their hearts and those who do not, then explains what he means by the chains of hell.

explicit_facts.text: Alma begins to expound these things to a man.
Alma says many may know God's mysteries but are commanded to impart according to the portion of God's word granted to people, based on their heed and diligence.
Alma says a person who hardens his heart receives a lesser portion of the word, while one who does not receives a greater portion.
Alma teaches that those who harden their hearts can come to know nothing of God's mysteries, be taken captive by the devil, and be led to destruction; he calls this the chains of hell.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma speaks to the unnamed man.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and clothing of Alma and his listener

spoken_dialogue.text: And therefore, he that will harden his heart, the same receiveth the lesser portion of the word;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma (son of Alma)

title: Alma on Judgment
summary: Alma refers to Amulek's words about death, immortality, and judgment. He warns of condemnation and says people must stand before God and acknowledge the justice of his judgments.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says Amulek has spoken about death, being raised to immortality, and being judged according to works.
Alma warns that those who harden their hearts against the word will be condemned.
Alma says words, works, and thoughts will condemn them.
Alma says people must stand before God and acknowledge that his judgments are just and that he is merciful.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance or number of any listeners

title: The second death
summary: Alma teaches that those who die in their sins face a second, spiritual death, describes their torments through comparisons, and says they cannot be redeemed according to God’s justice.

explicit_facts.text: Alma speaks of a second death, which is spiritual death, for those who die in their sins.
Alma compares their torments to a lake of fire and brimstone and says they will be chained down to everlasting destruction.
Alma says they cannot be redeemed according to God’s justice and cannot die.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal lake of fire, literal chains, Satan, or people visibly experiencing torment.

title: Antionah questions Alma
summary: After Alma finishes speaking, the people become more astonished. Antionah, a chief ruler among them, comes forth and questions Alma about rising from the dead and the scripture concerning Eden.

explicit_facts.text: Alma finishes speaking, and the people begin to be more astonished.
Antionah is a chief ruler among them and comes forth to speak to Alma.
Antionah asks about rising from the dead and changing from a mortal to an immortal state.
Antionah asks about scripture concerning cherubim and a flaming sword east of the garden of Eden, then says there was no possible chance that the first parents should live forever.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Antionah stands forward of the people while addressing Alma.

spoken_dialogue.text: What is this that thou hast said, that man should rise from the dead and be changed from this mortal to an immortal state that the soul can never die?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Antionah

spoken_dialogue.text: And thus we see that there was no possible chance that they should live forever.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Antionah

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Antionah mentions Eden while questioning scripture; the verses do not place the present exchange there.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the first parents, cherubim, or flaming sword as present in this exchange.
Do not invent additional speech or a response from Alma.

title: Alma Explains the Fall and Mortality
summary: Alma tells Antionah that Adam fell by partaking of the forbidden fruit. He teaches that death comes upon mankind and that this life is a time to repent and prepare to meet God.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says Adam fell by partaking of the forbidden fruit and that all mankind became a lost and fallen people.
Alma says that if Adam had partaken of the tree of life at that time, there would have been no death.
Alma says temporal death comes upon mankind, space was granted for repentance, and this life became a probationary state in which to prepare to meet God.

title: The plan of redemption
summary: Alma teaches that the plan of redemption makes resurrection possible. He says that without a preparatory state, partaking of the tree of life would have frustrated the plan, and that death is appointed before judgment.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says the plan of redemption, laid from the foundation of the world, brings about resurrection.
He says that living forever without a preparatory state would have frustrated the plan of redemption.
Alma says it is appointed that people die and after death come to judgment.

title: Mercy through the Only Begotten Son
summary: Alma recounts God's call to repent and not harden the heart, promising mercy and remission of sins through his Only Begotten Son to the repentant, while warning the hard-hearted will not enter his rest.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says God called on people in the name of his Son, promising mercy through his Only Begotten Son to those who repent and do not harden their hearts.
Those who repent and do not harden their hearts may claim mercy and remission of sins and enter God's rest.
Those who harden their hearts and do iniquity will not enter God's rest.
